note: Sign registry. Every entry carries its MUTCD 2009 Edition designation, category, shape, declared face and legend colors, a plain-language meaning, and a verbatim citation from the Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual. Where the manual shows a sign only as a captioned picture with no prose, the meaning is taken from the MUTCD and the reference is recorded in meaningSource — no meaning in this file is invented. Colors are palette tokens, not CSS: the rendering layer maps them. MUTCD designations were verified against the FHWA 2009 MUTCD chapter texts (Parts 2B, 2C, 2D, 2E, 2G, 2H, 2I, 6F, 7B, 8B, 9B). The palette is exactly the set of colors these faces paint: `npm run audit:signs` fails on a palette token no entry uses and on a rendered color no entry declares. "brown" (recreation and cultural interest guide signs) and "fluorescent-pink" (incident management) are taught here as color semantics — questions col-004 and col-007, manual-spine.md section 3.0 — but the manual illustrates no specific MUTCD-designated sign in either color, and minting a designation to justify a swatch is what practices D17 forbids; both were dropped from the face palette rather than faked into it. "silver" was dropped outright: it is not an MUTCD sign color.

signs.name: STOP
signs.meaning: Come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line; if you cannot see, edge forward to where you can and go only when it is safe.

citation.quote: you must bring your car to a complete stop, not going beyond the crosswalk

signs.name: YIELD
signs.meaning: Slow down and enter the intersection with caution; stop and wait when vehicles are approaching on the other roadway.

citation.quote: If you are sure no other cars are coming you need not come to a complete stop but you must slow down and enter the intersection with caution.

signs.name: ALL WAY plaque
signs.meaning: Mounted below a stop sign: all traffic approaching this intersection must stop.

citation.quote: Added below a stop sign. It means all traffic approaching this intersection must stop.

signs.name: SPEED LIMIT
signs.meaning: The maximum speed allowed on this stretch of road under ideal conditions.

citation.quote: These signs show the maximum speed allowed, the minimum speed required or a change in speed limit.

signs.name: MINIMUM SPEED plaque
signs.meaning: The minimum speed required under normal driving conditions; driving slower than this is against the law.

citation.quote: These signs show the maximum speed allowed, the minimum speed required or a change in speed limit.

signs.name: NO RIGHT TURN
signs.meaning: Right turns are prohibited at this location.

meaningSource.note: The manual teaches the circle-and-slash convention but does not describe this sign in prose.

citation.quote: Signs having a white background and a red circle and a line diagonally through them mean "NO" according to what is shown behind the red symbol.

signs.name: NO LEFT TURN
signs.meaning: Left turns are prohibited at this location.

meaningSource.note: Shown in the manual as a captioned picture ("NO LEFT TURN") under the circle-and-slash rule.

citation.quote: Signs having a white background and a red circle and a line diagonally through them mean "NO" according to what is shown behind the red symbol.

signs.name: NO TURNS
signs.meaning: No turns of any kind are permitted at this location — you must continue straight ahead.

meaningSource.note: Not described in prose by the manual; meaning taken from the MUTCD.

citation.quote: Signs having a white background and a red circle and a line diagonally through them mean "NO" according to what is shown behind the red symbol.

signs.name: NO U TURN
signs.meaning: U-turns are prohibited at this location.

meaningSource.note: Shown in the manual as a captioned picture ("NO U TURN") under the circle-and-slash rule.

citation.quote: Signs having a white background and a red circle and a line diagonally through them mean "NO" according to what is shown behind the red symbol.

signs.name: Mandatory movement lane control
signs.meaning: Traffic in this lane must move in the direction of the arrow shown.

citation.quote: While others indicate that traffic in the respective lanes must either move straight through or turn left.

signs.name: LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT
signs.meaning: The named lane is a mandatory turn lane; if you are in it, you must make that turn.

citation.quote: While others indicate that traffic in the respective lanes must either move straight through or turn left.

signs.name: High Occupancy Vehicle lane
signs.meaning: This lane is reserved for buses and vehicles carrying at least the number of occupants shown on the sign, during the hours posted.

citation.quote: This sign (High Occupancy Vehicle) indicates lanes reserved for buses and vehicles with the minimum number of occupants specified on the sign.

signs.name: BIKE LANE
signs.meaning: This lane is for bicycles only — drivers must never use it as a turning lane, a passing lane or for parking.

citation.quote: for bicycle use only, drivers must NEVER use this lane as a turning lane, passing lane or for parking

signs.name: DO NOT PASS
signs.meaning: Passing is not permitted from here; passing zones are set by how far ahead you can see.

citation.quote: These signs tell you where passing is not permitted. Passing areas are based on how far you can see ahead.

signs.name: PASS WITH CARE
signs.meaning: Marks the end of a no-passing restriction; passing is permitted but you must still judge the gap yourself.

meaningSource.note: The manual states the companion rule that the end of a no-passing zone does not mean passing is safe, but does not describe this sign face.

citation.quote: The end of a "no-passing zone" does not mean it is safe to pass. It means there is increased visibility ahead.

signs.name: SLOWER TRAFFIC KEEP RIGHT
signs.meaning: On a highway with more than one lane in each direction, slower traffic keeps to the extreme right lane; the left lanes are for passing and for turning left.

meaningSource.reference: MUTCD 2009 Ed. §2B.29 (R4-3 SLOWER TRAFFIC KEEP RIGHT)
meaningSource.note: The manual describes the rule on printed p.37 but does not print the sign's legend, so the designation is taken from the MUTCD. The near-identical KEEP RIGHT EXCEPT TO PASS legend is a different sign, R4-16 — this entry is deliberately not that one.

citation.quote: It means that you must drive in the extreme right lane unless you want to pass a slower moving car or make a left turn.

signs.name: KEEP RIGHT
signs.meaning: Keep to the right of the island, median or obstruction ahead.

meaningSource.note: The manual covers the keep-right rule in prose but does not describe this symbol sign.

citation.quote: Always drive on the right side of a two-lane highway except

signs.name: DO NOT ENTER
signs.meaning: You may not enter this roadway from where you are — traffic comes the other way.

citation.quote: RED is used only as a background color for STOP signs, multiple supplemental plates (FOUR-WAY or ALL WAY), DO-NOT-ENTER messages, WRONG WAY signs and on Interstate route markers.

signs.name: WRONG WAY
signs.meaning: You are travelling against traffic — stop and turn around.

citation.quote: you are on the wrong side of the road

signs.name: NO TRUCKS
signs.meaning: Trucks are prohibited on this roadway.

meaningSource.note: Shown in the manual as a captioned picture ("NO TRUCKS") under the circle-and-slash rule.

citation.quote: Signs having a white background and a red circle and a line diagonally through them mean "NO" according to what is shown behind the red symbol.

signs.name: NO BICYCLES
signs.meaning: Bicycles are prohibited on this roadway.

meaningSource.note: Shown in the manual as a captioned picture ("NO BICYCLES"); the manual separately states bicycles are barred from limited-access highways.

citation.quote: Bicyclists are prohibited on limited-access highways, expressways and certain other marked roadways.

signs.name: ONE WAY (horizontal arrow)
signs.meaning: Traffic on this street moves only in the direction of the arrow.

citation.quote: This sign tells you that you are approaching a one-way street and that you must not enter from the direction you are traveling.

signs.name: ONE WAY (vertical)
signs.meaning: Traffic on this street moves only in the direction shown; do not enter against it.

citation.quote: This sign tells you that you are approaching a one-way street and that you must not enter from the direction you are traveling.

signs.name: NO PARKING ANY TIME
signs.meaning: Parking is forbidden in the area where this sign is placed.

citation.quote: This sign tells you that, in the area where this sign is placed, parking is forbidden.

signs.name: Reserved accessible parking
signs.meaning: This space is reserved for vehicles displaying a disabled veteran or handicapped plate or placard, and only while transporting the person it was issued to.

citation.quote: Parking spaces displaying this blue sign are reserved for vehicles bearing disabled veteran or handicapped license plates, or a special handicapped decal.

signs.name: NO HITCHHIKING
signs.meaning: Soliciting a ride from the roadway is prohibited — in Tennessee it is illegal to stand on a roadway to solicit a ride.

citation.quote: In Tennessee, it is illegal to stand on a roadway to solicit a ride.

signs.name: NO TURN ON RED
signs.meaning: The turn on red that would otherwise be allowed here is prohibited; wait for a green indication.

citation.quote: Unless otherwise posted, you may turn right on red after coming to a complete stop and when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.

signs.name: ROAD CLOSED
signs.meaning: The road ahead is closed to through traffic; respect the barrier and take the detour.

citation.quote: respect "Road Closed" barriers posted to warn you of the danger

signs.name: Crossbuck (railroad grade crossing)
signs.meaning: Marks the exact location of railroad tracks at a grade crossing; yield to any train.

citation.quote: It is placed at all railroad grade crossings and shows exactly where the tracks are located.

signs.name: Number of tracks plaque
signs.meaning: Mounted below the crossbuck: the number of tracks at this crossing. More than one track means a second train may be hidden by the first.

citation.quote: They show the number of tracks at a particular crossing.

signs.name: School advance warning
signs.meaning: A school is ahead — slow down, drive with caution and watch for children.

citation.quote: It warns you to slow down, drive with caution and watch for children. This sign is placed as you approach a school.

signs.name: SCHOOL BUS STOP AHEAD
signs.meaning: A school bus loads and unloads ahead during the school season, so children are likely to be in the area.

citation.quote: This sign indicates that children are likely to be in the area with a school bus loading and unloading during the school season.

signs.name: SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT WHEN FLASHING
signs.meaning: The reduced school-zone speed limit applies while the yellow lights are flashing; exceeding it is treated as reckless driving.

citation.quote: This type of sign is controlled by a time clock and flashes yellow lights while illuminating the speed limit.

signs.name: Turn
signs.meaning: A sharp turn ahead, marked where the recommended speed is 30 m.p.h. or less.

citation.quote: The turn sign is used to mark turns with a recommended speed of 30 m.p.h. or less.

signs.name: Curve
signs.meaning: A curve ahead, marked where the recommended speed is between 30 and 55 m.p.h.

citation.quote: The curve sign is used to mark curves with recommended speeds in the range between 30 and 55 m.p.h.

signs.name: Reverse Turn
signs.meaning: Two turns in opposite directions less than 600 feet apart — right, then left.

citation.quote: The reverse turn sign is used to mark two turns in opposite directions that are less than 600 feet apart.

signs.name: Reverse Curve
signs.meaning: Two curves in opposite directions, close together — the gentler counterpart of the reverse turn sign.

meaningSource.note: The manual describes the reverse turn sign in prose but not the reverse curve; meaning taken from the MUTCD.

citation.quote: The reverse turn sign is used to mark two turns in opposite directions that are less than 600 feet apart.

signs.name: WINDING ROAD
signs.meaning: A series of turns or curves ahead — three or more changes of direction.

meaningSource.note: Shown in the manual only as a captioned picture ("WINDING ROAD"); meaning taken from the MUTCD.

citation.quote: Warning signs alert road users to conditions that might call for a reduction of speed or an action in the interest of safety and efficient traffic operations.

signs.name: One-direction large arrow
signs.meaning: Placed at a sharp change of direction: the roadway turns the way the arrow points.

meaningSource.note: Meaning taken from the MUTCD; the manual describes the related chevron sign in prose.

citation.quote: A sharp change in direction ahead

signs.name: Chevron alignment
signs.meaning: A sharp change in direction ahead; a line of chevrons guides you through the curve.

citation.quote: These Chevron signs displayed below are used to provide additional emphasis and guidance for a change in horizontal alignment.

signs.name: Advisory speed plaque
signs.meaning: Mounted under a warning sign: the recommended maximum safe speed for the condition ahead.

citation.quote: The smaller sign on the post beneath this sign is used to supplement warning signs. It gives you the recommended maximum safe speed.

signs.name: Cross road
signs.meaning: An intersection ahead where another road crosses yours; the black lines show its shape.

citation.quote: This sign tells you that you are approaching an intersection. The black lines show just what kind of intersection this is.

signs.name: Side road
signs.meaning: A side road joins from the direction shown; watch for vehicles entering.

meaningSource.note: The manual describes the intersection-warning family in prose but not this member; meaning taken from the MUTCD.

citation.quote: This sign tells you that you are approaching an intersection. The black lines show just what kind of intersection this is.

signs.name: T-intersection
signs.meaning: The road ahead ends at a through road — you must turn right or left, and be prepared to yield.

citation.quote: You must turn right or left. Be prepared to yield.

signs.name: Stop ahead
signs.meaning: There is a stop sign ahead that you cannot see yet — start slowing down now.

citation.quote: This sign indicates that there is a STOP sign just ahead that you cannot yet see. At this point, start to slow down.

signs.name: Yield ahead
signs.meaning: There is a yield sign ahead that you cannot see yet — start slowing down now.

citation.quote: This sign indicates that there is a YIELD sign just ahead that you cannot yet see. At this point, start to slow down.

signs.name: Signal ahead
signs.meaning: A traffic signal is ahead, often out of sight around a curve or over a rise.

citation.quote: A similar sign using a symbol shaped like a traffic light and the black arrow indicates there is a "traffic signal ahead."

signs.name: Merge
signs.meaning: Traffic is blending into your stream of travel; check behind and move over if you can to give them a clear path.

citation.quote: This sign alerts you to the possibility of traffic blending into the main stream of travel.

signs.name: Lane ends
signs.meaning: Your lane is ending — signal and merge, early rather than late.

citation.quote: This sign is warning of the lane ending and that drivers should merge left. Be sure to signal your intentions.

signs.name: Added lane
signs.meaning: A new lane is added for entering traffic, so the entering vehicles do not have to merge immediately.

citation.quote: The on-ramp becomes a new lane and the entering traffic does not need to merge immediately.

signs.name: Narrow bridge
signs.meaning: The bridge ahead is narrow and may require passing vehicles to slow down.

citation.quote: This sign tells you that the bridge is narrow and may require passing cars to reduce speeds.

signs.name: Divided highway begins
signs.meaning: The road ahead splits into separate roadways divided by a median — keep right and do not cross the median.

meaningSource.note: The manual explains divided highways and medians in prose but does not describe this sign face.

citation.quote: Do not drive within, across or over any median strip or barrier separating these roadways.

signs.name: TWO-WAY TRAFFIC
signs.meaning: The one-way or divided roadway ends ahead and you will meet oncoming traffic.

meaningSource.note: Shown in the manual only as a captioned picture ("TWO-WAY TRAFFIC"); meaning taken from the MUTCD.

citation.quote: Warning signs alert road users to conditions that might call for a reduction of speed or an action in the interest of safety and efficient traffic operations.

signs.name: SLIPPERY WHEN WET
signs.meaning: This surface is more slippery than usual when wet — reduce speed and avoid sudden inputs.

citation.quote: Some road surfaces are more slippery than others when wet. These roads usually have warning signs.

signs.name: BRIDGE ICES BEFORE ROAD
signs.meaning: This bridge freezes before the surrounding roadway, so it can be icy when the road is merely wet.

citation.quote: Usually, signs indicate that ice forms on bridges sooner than on the adjoining roads.

signs.name: FALLEN ROCKS
signs.meaning: Rocks may be lying in the road ahead — watch the roadway, not the hillside.

citation.quote: This sign warns of rocks that may be in the road, not of rocks which may strike you from overhead. Watch the roadway, not the hill.

signs.name: Bicycle warning
signs.meaning: Watch for bicyclists crossing or sharing the roadway ahead.

meaningSource.note: Shown in the manual as a captioned picture ("BIKE CROSSING"); meaning taken from the MUTCD.

citation.quote: On most roadways, bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as other roadway users

signs.name: Pedestrian warning
signs.meaning: Watch for people crossing on foot; pedestrian and crosswalk signs use fluorescent yellow-green.

citation.quote: FLUORESCENT YELLOW-GREEN IS THE COLOR FOR SCHOOL ZONES!

signs.name: Deer crossing
signs.meaning: Deer regularly cross here — if a collision is unavoidable, do not swerve.

citation.quote: Pay attention to "deer crossing" signs.

signs.name: CATTLE CROSSING
signs.meaning: Livestock may be crossing or on the roadway ahead.

meaningSource.note: Shown in the manual only as a captioned picture ("CATTLE CROSSING"); meaning taken from the MUTCD.

citation.quote: Warning signs alert road users to conditions that might call for a reduction of speed or an action in the interest of safety and efficient traffic operations.

signs.name: Equestrian crossing
signs.meaning: Horseback riders are common here — pass at a reasonable speed and distance, without sounding your horn.

citation.quote: Areas where horseback riding is common will usually be marked with an advisory sign.

signs.name: Horse-drawn vehicle warning
signs.meaning: Animal-drawn vehicles use this road; they have the same right to it as a motor vehicle.

citation.quote: Warning signs will be posted in areas where you are likely to find animal-drawn vehicles.

signs.name: LOW CLEARANCE
signs.meaning: Shows the distance from the road surface to the underside of the bridge or overpass ahead.

citation.quote: Shows the distance from road surface to the bottom of a bridge or overpass

signs.name: NO PASSING ZONE
signs.meaning: Marks the start of a no-passing zone; it is placed on the left side of the roadway.

citation.quote: A triangular No Passing Zone sign can also be used. These signs are yellow or orange and placed on the left side of the roadway.

signs.name: Runaway truck ramp
signs.meaning: An escape ramp ahead for trucks that have lost their brakes — never stop or park in one.

citation.quote: These ramps are designed to stop out-of-control trucks or buses going down step downgrades.

signs.name: Object marker (Type 3)
signs.meaning: Marks an obstruction close to the edge of the roadway, such as a bridge end or underpass abutment; the stripes slope down toward the side you should pass on.

citation.quote: These markers warn you of objects, not actually in the roadway, but so close to the edge of the road that need marking.

signs.name: ROAD WORK AHEAD
signs.meaning: Road work is ahead — slow down and be ready to stop; orange always means road work.

citation.quote: All temporary signs in work zones have an orange background and black letters or symbols.

signs.name: ONE LANE ROAD AHEAD
signs.meaning: Traffic ahead shares a single lane in both directions, usually under flagger control.

meaningSource.note: The manual covers flagger-controlled work zones in prose but does not describe this sign face.

citation.quote: In work areas, a person with a sign or flag may control traffic. You must obey the directions of these persons.

signs.name: RIGHT LANE CLOSED AHEAD
signs.meaning: The named lane closes ahead — merge early into the remaining open lanes.

citation.quote: You must begin to merge into the remaining open lane(s) well in advance of this sign.

signs.name: Flagger ahead
signs.meaning: A flagger is controlling traffic ahead; obey their signals, which carry the force of a traffic control device.

citation.quote: Flaggers, at most worksites, will be using paddles with the word stop on one side and slow on the other.

signs.name: Workers ahead
signs.meaning: People are working on or near the roadway ahead — be prepared to stop.

citation.quote: orange with black letters or symbols and warn you that people are working on or near the roadway

signs.name: END ROAD WORK
signs.meaning: The work zone restrictions end here; observe the posted work-zone signs until you reach it.

citation.quote: Observe the posted signs until you see the one that says "End Road Work".

signs.name: DETOUR
signs.meaning: Follow the marked alternative route around the closed road.

meaningSource.note: Shown in the manual as a captioned picture ("DETOUR") in the work-area section.

citation.quote: These construction, maintenance or emergency operations signs are generally diamond or rectangular shaped

signs.name: Distance plaque (1500 FEET)
signs.meaning: Mounted under a work-zone warning sign: how far ahead the condition begins. At highway speed, 1,500 feet is about 17 seconds away.

meaningSource.note: The manual illustrates the plaque only through its "Road Work 1500 Feet" example. A distance in FEET is W16-2P; W16-3P is the MILES plaque, which this entry previously and wrongly claimed. The registry id keeps its original spelling because questions.json references it and that file belongs to another piece.

citation.quote: If you see a sign that says "Road Work 1500 Feet", you'll be in that construction zone in 17 seconds!

signs.name: Railroad advance warning
signs.meaning: You are approaching a railroad grade crossing — slow down and be ready to stop; it is up to you to stop if a train is coming.

citation.quote: This circular sign always means that you are approaching a railroad grade crossing. You must slow down and be ready to stop.

signs.name: Railroad crossing at an intersection
signs.meaning: Tracks cross a roadway just beyond the intersection ahead — do not turn onto the tracks and stop short of them.

citation.quote: will be posted prior to intersections or crossroads where railroad tracks cross one of the roadways

signs.name: Emergency Notification System sign
signs.meaning: Carries the emergency number and crossing identifier to call if a vehicle is stalled or something is blocking the tracks.

citation.quote: The Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign, normally blue in color and may be located on the crossbuck post or signal post.

signs.name: Interstate route marker
signs.meaning: The route is part of the national system of interstate and defense highways.

citation.quote: Blue and red signs, like the one on the right, indicate that the route is part of the national system of interstate and defense highways.

signs.name: U.S. route marker
signs.meaning: A United States numbered highway route.

citation.quote: U.S. Route signs consists of black numerals on a white shield surrounded by a black background without a border.

signs.name: State primary route marker
signs.meaning: A Tennessee state route. The manual captions this marker a primary route, one that primarily connects cities; state secondary routes carry their own marker.

meaningSource.reference: MUTCD 2009 Ed. §2D.11 (M1-5 State Route marker; each State sets the outline)
meaningSource.note: The manual states only that one marker is "a state primary route" and the other "a state secondary route", and captions the primary route "Primarily Connects Cities". Tennessee draws the primary marker as a square. The claim that secondary routes connect smaller communities appears nowhere in the manual and has been removed.

citation.quote: PRIMARY ROUTE (Primarily Connects Cities)

signs.name: Milepost / reference location
signs.meaning: Marks your location along the route, so you can tell an emergency operator exactly where you are.

citation.quote: GREEN is used as a background color for guide signs (other than those using brown or white), mileposts

signs.name: EXIT gore sign
signs.meaning: Marks the point where the exit ramp separates from the through lanes.

meaningSource.note: The manual describes interstate exiting in prose but does not name this sign.

citation.quote: Exit signs are usually placed at least one mile ahead of the exit turn-off.

signs.name: EXIT ONLY panel
signs.meaning: A yellow EXIT ONLY panel on a green guide sign: all traffic in the lanes directly below the arrows must leave the highway.

citation.quote: If an interstate guide sign is marked with the above sign, all traffic in the lane(s) directly below the arrows MUST exit.

signs.name: Interstate guide sign (destination)
signs.meaning: Green guide signs give the information you need to pick the right lane and the right exit.

citation.quote: The background is green with white letters and/or numbers visible at some distance.

signs.name: Hospital (general service sign)
signs.meaning: Blue service signs direct motorists to facilities such as hospitals, rest areas, fuel, food and lodging.

citation.quote: The blue color of these signs directs motorists to service facilities.

signs.name: Gas (general service sign)
signs.meaning: Fuel is available at this exit; blue signs mean motorist services.

citation.quote: BLUE is used as a background color for information signs related to motorist services (including police services and rest areas) and the Emergency Route Marker.

signs.name: Food (general service sign)
signs.meaning: Restaurants are available at this exit; word-message versions of these signs are also used.

citation.quote: Word message signs will also be used to direct motorists to areas where service stations, restaurants and motels are available.
